description:
DECISION: stoa-rnews exits 0 (success) after processing a batch even if some individual articles were rejected (bad Message-ID, validation failure, pipeline permanent error). It exits non-zero only on fatal startup failures: config error, migration failure, or inability to parse the batch at all.

WHY RIGHT: This matches the documented semantics of the UUCP rnews tool. UUCP treats a non-zero exit from rnews as a signal that the batch was not processed and will queue it for retry. If stoa-rnews exited non-zero because one article out of 500 failed validation, UUCP would re-deliver all 500 articles. The transit pipeline would then deduplicate the 499 that already succeeded and attempt the bad one again — still failing, causing an infinite retry loop. Exiting 0 acknowledges receipt of the batch; per-article outcomes are logged and counted in structured log output. The exit-code semantics are documented in a comment at the top of rnews_main.rs.

ALTERNATIVES REJECTED:
- Exit non-zero if any article fails: creates retry loops; correct UUCP rnews implementations do not do this.
- Exit non-zero only on transient errors: reasonable in principle, but transient errors (storage unavailable) are indistinguishable at the batch level from permanent ones without inspecting all article results; the simpler policy is less error-prone.
title: rnews exits 0 even when individual articles are rejected (correct UUCP semantics)
